html:
SMTO-EXE-0184 — SMTO isn't allowed to open or save this Office file

GUID: 4078da60-ad3b-5417-b432-11f7e1b909c3
Slug: office-permission-denied
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: office

What happened

  • The Gateway (the helper program that works with files on a computer) runs as a user account on that computer, and that account isn't allowed to open your file or save into the chosen folder.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Move or copy the file into a normal folder of the user account that runs the Gateway on that computer, such as its Documents folder, then ask SMTO to use that location. The Gateway can only open files its own account is allowed to read.
  2. Ask SMTO to save the result without naming a folder, so it appears under Artifacts in SMTO's reply, or pick a folder that already exists and that account can write to. SMTO can't create the new file in a folder that account isn't allowed to write to.
  3. If the file is on a shared or protected drive, ask the person who manages that computer to give the Gateway's account read and write access. Access to shared and protected locations is controlled outside SMTO.

What success looks like

  • SMTO reads the file and reports the new file it created.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the full file location, to the person who manages SMTO or that computer. Don't make the folder open to everyone just to fix this.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Local Office file access raised PermissionError under the Gateway's operating-system account while reading the source or writing the output.

What this means

  • Local Office/File access raised PermissionError under the Gateway account. Office workers treat document content as untrusted data and never execute macros or formulas. Publication creates a separate output under existing File policy; retain revision and effect facts before any new write.

Why this can happen

  • Local Office/File access raised PermissionError under the Gateway account.

How to diagnose it

  • Identify whether source reading, auxiliary input or output-directory access was denied; preserve current File policy.

How to fix it

  • Identify the OS account the Gateway runs as and check its read permission on the source file and write permission on the existing output directory (ACLs, ownership, protected folders). Grant access or move the file, or omit output_path so the result is published to the run artifact directory.
  • Choose a readable source and a writable existing output directory on the selected Gateway.

Retry and execution caution

  • Choose a readable source and a writable existing output directory on the selected Gateway.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended source is readable and the new output can be created in an authorized existing directory.

What not to do

  • Never automatically replay uncertain writes or execute embedded document content.

Technical notes

  • Office workers treat document content as untrusted data and never execute macros or formulas. Publication creates a separate output under existing File policy; retain revision and effect facts before any new write.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
